findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food manager to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, PIC will ensure a certified food manager is brought in. Ensure a certified food manager is available within the facility during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed kitchen hand sinks to be missing paper towels. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm Cl. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Triple sink will be used until dish machine is serviced. Ensure dish machine is sanitizing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed open juices to be stored in a cooler at 70F. Discussed with PIC, cooler is observed to be down and items were discarded. Any juices in the future will be stored in walk in cooler. Ensure any TCS item is cold held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.comment: Inspectors observed an opened bottle of stir fry sauce with “Refrigerate After Opening” on the label in the dry storage. The person-in-charge was reminded of this violation from the previous routine inspection conducted on January 12, 2026 and the sauce was voluntarily discarded today. Ensure time/temperature for safety foods are stored at 5°C (41°F) or less after opening.

PIC was informed and the food items were willingly discarded. Inspectors will do a spot check on 01/22/2026. Ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored at 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following to have an accumulation of food residue and other debris:

- The microwave has accumulation of food residue and grease.
- The big container for storing utensils has accumulation of food debris and grease. Some utensils are stained with the debris found in the container.
- The shelf at the entrance of the walk-in cooler has accumulation of grease. 

The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed. Ensure that food residue and other debris are regularly cleaned from the food and non-food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the caulking behind the sink wall and coving in the bathroom to be missing. PIC was informed. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the employee handling food to not have a food handler certificate. PIC was educated on the importance of employees handling foods to be certificated. Ensure food handlers employed must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed multiple pests to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, pest control unit will be called to service facility. Ensure facility is kept pest free.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector observed two bags of ice stored on the floor of the walk in freezer. Bags of ice were discarded as they will no longer be needed. Take care to properly protect food. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the top of the knife block to be soiled with crumbs and dust. Clean knife block and maintain it clean in order to protect clean knives from contamination.


4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following non-food contact surfaces soiled: 1) heat bar edge 2) catch tray for the stove top 3) bottom shelf of the prep table holding pans next to the walk in cooler and 4) the air conditioner. Clean and maintain the area free of dust, crumbs and soil. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the floor behind the cooking equiplent to be soiled with some food debris. Clean and maintain the area free of food debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a grey hoodie and black apron hanging on the end of the food storage shelf. Find proper storage for personal possessions. 

6-305.11: (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.
